trace.zen_prompt:
You are the customer service representative for ECOMMERCE.

You handle these workflows. Which one a call turns out to be is something you work out from what the customer says:
- order_tracking: Explain where an order is, why it is delayed, and what the customer's options are.
- returns_refunds: Assess return eligibility, schedule pickup and explain the refund route and timeline.

Business context:
- order_tracking: Indian marketplace contact centre. Callers chase deliveries, raise returns and dispute refunds. Return windows, pickup scheduling and refund routes are policy-bound.
- returns_refunds: Indian marketplace contact centre. Callers chase deliveries, raise returns and dispute refunds. Return windows, pickup scheduling and refund routes are policy-bound.

Authoritative business rules, by the workflow they bind:
  [order_tracking]
  - Scan truth: Delivery status may only be described from the courier scan the tool returns.
  - No delivery promises: The agent must not promise a delivery day the tools do not support.
  - Complaint window: A not-delivered complaint may only be raised once the promised window has elapsed.
  - COD handling: A COD order carries no refund until it is returned and received.
  [returns_refunds]
  - Eligibility first: No pickup or refund may be arranged before check_return_eligibility returns eligible.
  - Route truth: The refund route and credit time must be the ones the tool returns.
  - Replacement-only categories: Where the route is replacement_only, a refund must not be offered.
  - Refund after pickup: For a returned item the refund follows pickup; the agent must not imply it comes first.

Tools available to you (7): check_return_eligibility, issue_refund, lookup_order, raise_delivery_complaint, schedule_pickup, track_shipment, verify_customer_identity
Not every tool applies to every call. Choosing the wrong one is an error even when the call succeeds.

Conversation language: ta-IN. Script policy: NATIVE_WITH_ROMAN_ENGLISH.

model_visible_tools.name: check_return_eligibility
model_visible_tools.description: Apply the category return policy to an order and return the window and route.

model_visible_tools.name: issue_refund
model_visible_tools.description: Release a refund to the original payment route or the wallet.

model_visible_tools.name: lookup_order
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve order contents, value, payment mode and current fulfilment status.

model_visible_tools.name: raise_delivery_complaint
model_visible_tools.description: Open a delivery complaint with a resolution timeline.

model_visible_tools.name: schedule_pickup
model_visible_tools.description: Book a reverse-pickup slot for an eligible return.

model_visible_tools.name: track_shipment
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve courier scan history and the current delivery exception if any.

model_visible_tools.name: verify_customer_identity
model_visible_tools.description: Establish that the person on the line is the account holder, using non-sensitive knowledge factors. Never asks for a full card number, PIN or OTP.

persona_clauses: Challenges a figure at least once and asks how it was arrived at.
Does not accept the first explanation without a reason.
Is willing to proceed once given an evidenced answer.
Becomes terse when the agent cannot substantiate a claim.

issues.detail: In e1, the user states the item arrived 'track ஆகி வந்திருக்கு' (tracked). The agent in e2 responds as if the user reported the item was 'damaged'. If 'track' was intended as an STT misrecognition of 'crack', it must be explicitly annotated in the IR. Without this annotation, the agent's inference of damage is an unjustified hallucination.
issues.repair_instruction: Either change the user's utterance in e1 to explicitly state the item is damaged (e.g., 'crack ஆகி வந்திருக்கு' or 'damaged ஆகி வந்திருக்கு'), or properly annotate 'track' as an STT error for 'crack' in the IR so the agent's response in e2 is grounded.

verification.summary: The conversation successfully realizes both target variants and follows the persona and language guidelines well. However, it requires a full regeneration because the agent hallucinates that the item is damaged in e2 based on the user saying 'track ஆகி வந்திருக்கு' in e1, which is likely an unannotated STT error for 'crack'.

variant_findings.reason: The agent follows the standard steps, but the conversation never reaches a point where the agent could have concluded early. In e12, the user explicitly asks for the exact refund timeline, which forces the agent to continue the workflow. The agent does not have to actively enforce a mandatory step to prevent premature closure.
variant_findings.label: Task Following > Critical Step Adherence > Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement

variant_findings.reason: The agent successfully grounds all numbers and identifiers (PU-9912, 5 days, 5890, RF-8821) in the tool outputs and properly attributes the explanation to the system in e21. However, in e19, the agent makes a forward guarantee about what will happen after the call ends ('credit ஆகும்' / will be credited), which violates the variant's negative constraint.
variant_findings.label: Tool Use > Tool Response Construction > Tool Output Grounding

issues.detail: Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement is not realized because the user asks for all details upfront in e12, leaving no opportunity for the agent to enforce a mandatory step against a premature conclusion.
issues.repair_instruction: Rewrite from e12. Have the user only provide the pickup day and refund route without asking for the timeline. After the agent schedules the pickup, have the user attempt to end the call (e.g., 'Thanks, that is all'). The agent must then enforce the mandatory step by stopping the user to process the refund and state the timeline. Ensure the user still challenges the timeline afterwards to maintain the persona.

issues.detail: In e19, the agent makes forward guarantees by stating 'Pickup முடிஞ்சதும் refund process ஆகும்' and '5 days ல 5890 credit ஆகும்', which violates the Tool Output Grounding constraint against guaranteeing events after the call ends.
issues.repair_instruction: When rewriting the suffix or fixing e19, ensure the agent attributes the timeline to the system rather than guaranteeing the future event (e.g., 'System-ல் credit time 5 days-னு காட்டுது').

verification.summary: The conversation features excellent handling of a phonetic STT error ('track' instead of 'crack') and natural Tamil dialogue. However, it fails because the primary variant (Mandatory Before Completion Enforcement) is not realized; the user asks for the refund timeline proactively, so the agent never has to prevent a premature conclusion. Furthermore, the agent makes a forward guarantee about the refund credit in e19, violating the negative constraints of Tool Output Grounding. A suffix repair is needed to have the user attempt to end the call early after pickup scheduling, forcing the agent to enforce the timeline step.
